title: Follow the Dollar
bannerText: Figures come from the FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget. The county has not posted the adopted budget book yet; we will update when it does.
note: Checked on 2026-11-22 against the FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan (Vols. 1-3). The adopted book was not yet posted. Department amounts are operating budget figures from Appendix A. Amounts are in millions of dollars.

sources.name: Countywide property tax
sources.blurb: Paid by property owners across the whole county.
sources.restriction: Countywide property tax revenue goes into the Countywide General Fund.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 1, Appendix C, p. 134 (General Property Tax)

sources.name: Fire Rescue District property tax
sources.blurb: A separate property tax in the area Fire Rescue serves.
sources.restriction: The fire district tax can only pay for Fire Rescue.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 2, Fire Rescue, Operating Financial Summary, p. 214 (Fire Ad Valorem District Tax)

sources.name: Library District property tax
sources.blurb: A separate property tax in the area the county libraries serve.
sources.restriction: The library district tax can only pay for the county library system.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 2, Library, Operating Financial Summary, p. 261 (Library Ad Valorem District Tax)

sources.name: State sales tax (county share)
sources.blurb: The part of Florida's sales tax that the state shares with the county.
sources.restriction: The county's share of state sales tax goes to its two general funds.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 1, Appendix C, p. 134 and Appendix D, p. 135 (State Sales Tax)

sources.name: Transit surtax (half-penny)
sources.blurb: The half-cent sales surtax for the People's Transportation Plan. This is the part in the transit operating budget.
sources.restriction: The transit surtax can only pay for transportation under the People's Transportation Plan.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 3, Transportation and Public Works, Operating Financial Summary, p. 59 (PTP Sales Tax Revenue)

sources.name: Water and sewer bills
sources.blurb: Retail and wholesale water and wastewater charges.
sources.restriction: Water bill revenue can only pay for the water and sewer system.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 3, Water and Sewer, Operating Financial Summary, p. 112 (Retail Water, Retail Wastewater, Wholesale Water, Wholesale Wastewater)

sources.name: Garbage and trash fees
sources.blurb: Household collection fees and disposal fees.
sources.restriction: Garbage fees can only pay for trash collection and disposal.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 3, Solid Waste Management, Operating Financial Summary, p. 14 (Collection Fees and Charges, Disposal Fees and Charges)

sources.name: Airport fees and rents
sources.blurb: Aviation fees, commercial operations and rents at MIA and the county's other airports.
sources.restriction: Airport money has to stay with the airport system under federal rules.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 2, Aviation, Operating Financial Summary, p. 48 (Aviation Fees and Charges, Commercial Operations, Rental Income)

sources.name: Seaport fees
sources.restriction: Seaport fees can only pay for PortMiami.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 2, Seaport, Operating Financial Summary, p. 118 (Proprietary Fees)

sources.name: Tourist and restaurant taxes
sources.blurb: Hotel room taxes plus food and beverage taxes. State law lists what each one can pay for.
sources.restriction: Tourist and restaurant taxes can only go to uses state law lists, like tourism, culture, convention facilities and homeless services.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 1, Appendix M, p. 169 (FY 2026-27 estimates for all five taxes)

sources.name: Federal grants
sources.blurb: Money the federal government awards for specific programs.
sources.restriction: Federal grants can only pay for the programs they were awarded for.
sources.citation: Miami-Dade County FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and Multi-Year Capital Plan, Vol. 1, Appendix A, p. 116 (Grand Total, FY 2026-27 Federal Funds column)
